step_by_step_reasoning:
1) Confirmed there are no applicable knowledge-base helper functions, so all work will be done with Playwright calls.
2) Built a robust origin (using page.url) to construct absolute URLs for order detail pages if needed.
3) Located the main orders table by filtering tables that contain the 'Order #' link in the header.
4) Determined column indices for Status, Bill to Name (customer), and Action by inspecting the header row (using .get_by_role on header cells). Used textual heuristics if link-based detection fails.
5) Set the Status filter combobox in the filter row to 'Canceled' (falling back to 'Cancelled' if necessary) and clicked the Search button via the specific table that contains the Search button (use full path as required).
6) Determined the total number of pages by finding the pagination table that contains the 'Go to Next page' link and parsing the "of N pages" text. Defaulted to 1 page if parsing fails.
7) Iterated a finite number of pages (1..total_pages). For each page, collected data rows (skipping header and filter rows) and extracted canceled rows' href (View link or any link), customer name (Bill to Name cell when present), and date text where possible.
   - Note: I avoided infinite loops and used a deterministic page count loop.
8) If canceled orders list empty, returned 0.00 early.
9) Counted cancellations per customer using grid names. If the top customer was unknown or there were unknowns, visited detail pages for orders lacking a customer to resolve actual customer names. This avoids relying on potentially missing grid data.
10) Identified the customer with the most cancellations (most_customer).
11) Built a candidate list of that customer's canceled orders (using grid names where available; verifying detail pages when grid lacked a name).
12) For each candidate order, visited its detail page, verified the customer when necessary, and used page.evaluate() to extract two pieces of information from the DOM: createdAt (ms since epoch) and item_total (sum of product price * qty) using robust heuristics to find an items table or fallback subtotal text.
13) If createdAt could not be found on the detail page, attempted to parse the grid date_text for that row; otherwise used current time as a last-resort.
14) From all detailed orders for that customer, found the most recent createdAt and summed item_total for any orders within 1 second of that timestamp (to handle potential formatting/precision differences). Printed and returned the summed value formatted to two decimals.

- Avoided calling Locator objects like functions; always used Locator methods correctly with await where needed.
- Re-validated locators after navigation since the DOM may change between pages.
- Did not attempt to interact with Advanced Reporting.
